title: Новость о Нагиеве и болезни Шефа  (News of Nagiyev and the Chef's Illness)

segments.t: After promising to help Sasha clean up the water damage, Max arrives at Claude Monet for the morning briefing. Nagiyev announces to the staff that he and Kristina have called off their divorce, and then breaks the news that Chef Barinov is in the hospital.
Не вижу сволочи радости в ваших глазах.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'Well, we will sort it out tomorrow.' Notice the reflexive suffix on the verb meaning 'we'll sort it out', turning the action back on the subject. Max answers right away.
'I will clean everything up.' The meaning hinges on 'I' working together with 'will clean up' in spoken Russian.
'Could you not have turned off the water?' Kristina addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'turn off'.
'I specifically asked you to.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'asked'. Kristina answers right away.
'Attention everyone, Kristina and I are together.' In Russian, the idea of 'attention' flows naturally into 'together' without extra filler words.
'There will be no divorce.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'divorce' before landing on 'will'.
'Yesterday we...' The grammar packs 'we' and 'yesterday' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Max answers right away.
'That is not what matters right now, guys.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'not' and finishing on 'kids'.
'Anyway.' Kristina brings out the contrast between 'short' and 'short' in a few short words.
Не вижу сволочи радости в ваших глазах.
'I do not see any joy in your eyes, you scoundrels.' The negative particle sits right before the verb meaning 'see' to negate the statement. Kristina answers right away.
'Wait, what happened to Vitya?' The grammar packs 'so' and 'Vitya' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'All right then.' Max anchors the line on 'come on', while 'really?!' completes the thought.
'So, guys, hand me a broom.' In Russian, the idea of 'therefore' flows naturally into 'a broom' without extra filler words. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
